Quick start

How to use this tool

  1. Choose percentage assessment weights or relative module credits.
  2. Add one row per completed assessment or module; enter its percentage score and weight.
  3. Calculate. For incomplete percentage weights, read the current average separately from course contribution.

Planning estimate · Check your syllabus for official grading rules.

See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Weighted average = Σ(Score × Weight) ÷ Σ(Weight)

A worked example

Coursework of 80% at a 40% weight and an exam of 70% at a 60% weight give (80 × 40 + 70 × 60) ÷ 100 = 74%. If only the coursework is finished, its current average is 80%, its contribution to the full course is 32 percentage points, and 60% remains ungraded.

Before you use the result

Percentage weights must total no more than 100%. The tool normalizes completed work to calculate the current average; it does not silently treat unfinished assessments as zero. In module-credit mode, 65% in a 20-credit module and 75% in a 40-credit module give 71.67%. This is a credit-weighted mark, not an official UK degree classification. Institution rules about years, reassessments, borderline marks and exclusions still apply.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Do the weights need to add up to 100?

Only a complete set of percentage assessment weights should total 100%. Credit or relative weights do not need to total 100.

Can I use UK university module credits?

Yes, choose module credits and enter each module mark and credit value. This calculates an average only, without awarding a degree class.

Should I enter ungraded work as zero?

Only enter zero when a zero has actually been awarded. Leave ungraded work out and check how much weight remains.
